title: Iterator vs ListIterator: forward-only vs bidirectional, add/set during iteration
shortTitle: What is the difference between Iterator and ListIterator?
keyPoints: Iterator is forward-only and works on any Collection; it supports hasNext(), next(), and remove()
ListIterator extends Iterator for Lists only; it adds backward traversal, add(), set(), and index tracking
ListIterator is the only way to safely add or replace elements during iteration without CME
ListIterator can start at any index: list.listIterator(5) begins before the element at index 5
LinkedList benefits most from ListIterator because add/remove at the current position is O(1)
Iterator is the safer default for simple traversal; ListIterator is for bidirectional or in-place modification

s1_definition.oneliner: Iterator traverses any Collection forward-only with remove(); ListIterator extends it for Lists with backward traversal, add(), set(), and index tracking.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Iterator** (`java.util.Iterator<E>`): works on any Collection, forward-only with `hasNext()`/`next()`, can only `remove()` the last returned element
- **ListIterator** (`java.util.ListIterator<E>`): extends Iterator for `List` only, adds `hasPrevious()`/`previous()` for backward traversal, `add(e)` to insert, `set(e)` to replace, and `nextIndex()`/`previousIndex()` for position tracking
- ListIterator is the only safe way to add or modify elements during iteration
- Can start at any position: `list.listIterator(index)`
s1_definition.analogy: Iterator is like reading a bank statement page by page from front to back – you can only go forward and can tear out (remove) a page. ListIterator is like having a bookmark that moves both forward and backward, letting you insert new pages, replace the current page, and check the page number at any time.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Iterator vs ListIterator

  Iterator:      → A → B → C → (end)
                 forward only, remove only

  ListIterator:  ← A ↔ B ↔ C → (end)
                 forward + backward
                 add, set, remove
                 nextIndex, previousIndex

  ListIterator cursor positions:
  |A|B|C|      ← cursor is BETWEEN elements
  ^             listIterator(0): before A
    ^           listIterator(1): before B
      ^         listIterator(2): before C
        ^       listIterator(3): after C
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Iterator is the basic forward-only cursor that works on any Collection. ListIterator extends it for Lists with backward traversal, in-place add and set, and index tracking. ListIterator is the only safe way to add or modify elements during iteration.

In the National Bank of India's compliance module, Rajesh uses a ListIterator to walk through the transaction list and insert audit markers after each entry. Because ListIterator.add() is safe during iteration, no ConcurrentModificationException occurs, and on LinkedList the insertion is O(1).

Remember one sentence: Iterator goes forward and can only remove; ListIterator goes both ways and can add, set, and remove – use it when you need to modify a List during traversal.
